title: Density and distance from the city centre

draft.title: Density and distance from the city centre
card: Population density is the number of people living in a given area, such as per square kilometre. A city does not have the same density everywhere.
The central business district (CBD) is the centre of a city, with offices, shops and services. Land there is costly and in short supply, so many people live in apartment buildings.
Moving away from the CBD, land is cheaper and there is more room. Houses with yards become common, so density usually falls.
The rural-urban fringe is the edge, where the city meets farmland or bush. Density is usually lowest here, with large blocks and open land.
draft.remember: Density is usually highest near the CBD and falls toward the edge of the city.

a.q: Moving from the CBD to the rural-urban fringe of a large Australian city, how does population density usually change?
opts: It falls, because there is more land per person
It rises, because land is cheaper further out
It stays the same, because the city is one area
It rises, because there are more houses with yards
a.why: Land further from the CBD is cheaper and more plentiful, so homes are spread out and density usually falls. Cheaper land does not mean higher density: it lets people live on larger blocks.
a.clue: Think about how much land each home takes up.

b.q: Sam compares two suburbs of Perth. One is 2 km from the CBD and full of apartment blocks. The other is 40 km out, on the rural-urban fringe, with large blocks. Which statement is most likely true?
opts: The suburb near the CBD has the higher density
The suburb on the fringe has the higher density
Both suburbs have about the same density
The fringe has more people on each square kilometre
b.why: Land near the CBD is costly and scarce, so many people live in apartments and density is high. On the fringe, large blocks spread people out, so density is lower.
b.clue: Which suburb has apartments packed close together?

a.best: It falls, because there is more land per person

b.best: The suburb near the CBD has the higher density

problems.detail: Two wrong options mean the same thing: 'The suburb on the fringe has the higher density' and 'The fringe has more people on each square kilometre'. Since only one answer can be right, a student can rule out both without knowing the idea, which leaves an easy two-way choice.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. In question b, two distractors say the same thing, so students can eliminate both without understanding density; replace one with a different plausible wrong option.
